Nice forward — thanks. Quick guardrails and a suggested play:

Guardrails:
- Maximum incremental discount we can offer off list for mid-term additions without legal amendment: 25% if it is a hard commit and extends their term or adds non-refundable premium.
- Anything >25% needs executive approval and a revenue protection plan.

Suggested customer-facing structure (fastest to close):
1) Blended banding: first 200 incremental seats at 25%, next 300 at 10%. This protects unit economics and rewards immediate uplift.
2) Co-term: yes — push to co-term to 2028-01-31 with a one-time true-up at co-term to normalize pricing.
3) Billing: bill incremental seats at the discounted rate going forward; provide a separate one-off onboarding credit ($10,000) applied within the first invoice cycle.
4) ARR / accounting: propose an invoice credit approach (book full ARR, then send a one-time credit) OR alternatively bill at discount and run a 6-month revenue true-up; finance will advise which is cleaner.

I'll side with the blended banding above — gives us room and feels competitive. Karthik, can you run the back-of-envelope on ARR impact and proposed credit amortization (if any)?

Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Manager

Attaching a quick calc (Discount_Calc_Q2.xlsx). Notes from finance: 

1) For ARR recognition cleanliness we prefer to bill at list and apply a customer credit amortized over the remaining months of the contract. That keeps ARR intact and avoids restating revenue.
2) If we bill at a discounted rate instead, we'll need a short memo capturing the discount rationale (sales approved) to satisfy audit. Fine, but it increases bookkeeping we might avoid.
3) Proposed conservative structure that balances sales/the customer and finance:
   - Deal id: NB-2027-004 (please reference in PO)
   - Blended banding per Marcus — apply a one-time credit equal to (weighted average discount * incremental ARR) and amortize that credit monthly across the remaining 7 months to co-term.
   - Example: blended effective discount = 17.5% -> credit = $XXX,XXX -> amortize across months. See sheet for numbers.

Also recommend a $7,500 onboarding credit (middle ground) rather than the $10k Marcus proposed.

If legal wants to keep it very simple we can do a 30-day pro-rata invoice for the new seats at list and then reconcile at co-term. That avoids a long amendment and is low friction for procurement.
